issues.description: The problem statement refers to a Farm method named printFarmSong() (UML and task text), but both the template and the solution implement and reference a method named singFarmSong(). This name/signature mismatch between the specification and the code can confuse students about which method to implement and may cause tests or instructions to appear inconsistent.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong() (and any mentions of printFarmSong()) so it matches the template/solution, or (B) rename the method in the template and solution to printFarmSong() so it matches the specification. Ensure all example usages (e.g., in Main and task descriptions) use the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a Farm method named printFarmSong(), while both the template and the solution implement and refer to singFarmSong(). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual operation (playing/singing the farm song) can confuse students who search for printFarmSong() in the starter code or follow the UML, but find singFarmSong() instead.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the implemented methods to printFarmSong() in the template and solution, or update the problem statement and UML to refer to singFarmSong(). Prefer updating the problem statement/UML to singFarmSong() to match existing code and Main usage, or alternatively rename singFarmSong() -> printFarmSong() in both template and solution.
